messages:
sam: Heads-up — design question about routing headers for SDKs. We need a concise set of headers/query params to let clients hint region/tier and enable debug traces without opening up user-level escape hatches.

tara: +1. Current options are messy (region_hint, X-RW-Region, ?zone=). Can we standardize a single canonical surface?

liam: Proposal: conservative header names: `X-Redwood-Region`, `X-Redwood-Tier`, `X-Redwood-Debug`. Prefer headers over query params for sensitive flags.

nisha: Agree on headers. Also we should allow `region_hint` as a query param for browser clients that can't set custom headers easily. But header should take precedence.

sam: Precedence rules: 1) Explicit header wins. 2) query param if header missing. 3) account-level default from console. Also fallback: if requested region is unavailable route by policy (region->tier->variant). Need to document fallback order.

liam: Fallback order idea: same-region compatible-model -> cross-region same-tier -> cross-region lower-tier -> degrade to hosted-low-cost variant. We should tag which fallback path was used in telemetry.

tara: Telemetry needs fields: routing_path, final_region, final_tier, fallback_reason, variant_used. Also include token_id or org_id for quota checks (scrubbed in logs).

sam: About debug flags: `X-Redwood-Debug: route=explain,trace=true` — sensitive. Only allow for internal tokens or orgs with debug entitlement. For public keys, ignore debug header and log that it was suppressed.

nisha: SDK behaviour: SDK default should set `X-Redwood-Region` from user preferred region in config. CLI/servers can override explicitly. Web SDK: use `?region_hint=` fallback.

liam: Small example for docs:
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1
X-Redwood-Tier: enterprise
X-Redwood-Debug: route=explain
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```
Response headers should include: `X-Redwood-Routed-Region`, `X-Redwood-Routed-Tier`, `X-Redwood-Fallback-Path` (comma list), and `X-Redwood-Routing-Trace-ID`.

tara: One open question: quotas. If user hints region A but their quota for region A is exhausted, do we charge their quota bucket for attempted region or for the final region? We should charge final region, but surface attempted region in billing records for debugging.

sam: I think final-region charging is best for customers. Internally store attempted_region and final_region in usage rows. Also quota checks should be simulated in canary rollout so we don't accidentally route paid traffic to lower SLAs.

nisha: UX for rollouts: in console, show a small toggle in rollout policies: "Honor client region hints" (on/off), and an explain button that shows typical fallback chain and sample telemetry.

liam: Security note: header names should be vetted for conflicts with proxies and CDNs. `X-Redwood-*` is safe, but mention that some edge proxies strip unknown headers. Add `region_hint` query param as reliable fallback.

sam: dev-bot: deploy-plan created for header-surface-change. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/routing/pull/428 :eyes:

nisha: Action items: 1) liam create RFC doc w/ header names + precedence + examples. 2) tara add telemetry fields to schema. 3) sam add console UX mockup. 4) liam gate debug header to internal entitlements.

sam: Cool. If no objections I'll draft RFC by EOD and add to eng docs. :thumbsup:

liam: No objections from me. Quick reminder to include integration tests for fallback precedence and metrics emission.

nisha: Also include a short e2e test that asserts `X-Redwood-Debug` is ignored for public tokens.

tara: Thanks folks — merging this into the roadmap.

dev-bot: deploy-plan updated, job queued: routing-header-rfc (job id: 2026-742).
